newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher, continuing uptrend.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher, continuing uptrend.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Monday, continuing their recent uptrend tied to physical power prices driven higher by cooling demand in the Southwest.
"We're continuing where we left off," said one Houston futures trader,

In OTC business, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $19.40-19.85 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Friday's settlement at $19.53, and June Palo Verde (PV) $25.90-26.25 compared with Friday's close at $25.70.
Market sources said the complex could propel to new highs again from strong cash prices, steady natural gas futures and hot weather in parts of the Southwest.
In the daily physical market, next-day firm, peak deliveries at COB were quoted at $24.00-26.00, while those at PV at $38.00-40.00.
As of 1013 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures were up 0.1 cent at $2.250 per million British thermal units.
The latest six to 10 day forecasts showed most of the Southwest would remain warm and wet, while a system of dry heat would keep the interior section hot.
In the Northwest, weather conditions would stay mild and dry into next week with readings in the 60s-70s F.
Market sources warned the complex could came under downward pressure from short-term profit-taking.
